details:
@wanzforme/bails is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that silently subscribes the installer's own WhatsApp account to WhatsApp Channels chosen by the publisher. When the socket connects, code in lib/Socket/newsletter.js sends the WhatsApp w:mex FOLLOW query for the channel ID(s) 120363380357951328@newsletter (stored base64-encoded), using the victim's authenticated session and without telling them. Same behaviour as the PhantomSub family (MAL-2026-17342).

## Source: amazon-inspector (24423e3b5883bd690c8cd8ee1bd60786bce4212836699f49d23057aca66bd2b6)
package.json declares `"libsignal": "github:wanzchil/libsignal-node"`, resolving the dependency from the HEAD of a GitHub repository with no tag, commit SHA, or integrity hash. On `npm install`, npm fetches whatever that repository currently contains and executes any lifecycle scripts it defines, inside the installer's environment. The content at HEAD can be changed at any time by the repository owner, so the bytes executed on the installer are mutable and not verified against the published tarball. The repository is under the same author account as the package, but off-registry sourcing bypasses the registry's integrity and audit surface regardless of ownership. A a static rule also matched network/command tokens (`ping`, `GET`) in lib/Utils/generics.js, but those appear in ordinary utility code paths rather than an install-time exec sink; the install-time-rce exposure comes from the dependency source itself.
